passage:
An apartment building installed delivery boxes so packages could be stored safely when residents were not home.
The boxes reduced missing packages, but new problems appeared. Some residents forgot to pick up items, leaving no space for others. Others ordered large things that did not fit.
The building created rules for pickup time and package size.
The delivery boxes worked better after that.
Modern convenience often depends on shared systems. A system can be well designed and still fail if users think only of themselves.
The box at the entrance was not just storage. It was a test of community behavior in the age of online shopping.
